title: Phaedo User Configuration
description: The §5 User Configuration artifact — the subject-AUTHORED sibling of the fingerprint (Phaedo Protocol v0.1 §5). Authored content: stated once, no producer confidence score, applied VERBATIM, never inferred (§5.6 — inferred edits are forbidden). This schema is the CANONICAL home of the §5.2 standing-instruction shape ($defs/standing_instruction); fingerprint.schema.json's standing_rules[] (the v0.1 A-home, Proposal 0007) $refs it, so the two homes cannot drift during the v0.2 migration. The wrapper key phaedo_user_configuration is the vault/payload key, mirroring phaedo_fingerprint; the inner object is the §5.1 document. Paired to exactly one fingerprint via fingerprint_id (§5.4) — a configuration without a paired fingerprint is invalid. Rides the same envelope (§7) with artifact_kind 'user_configuration' and the distinct key-derivation context phaedo:config:enc (§5.5). Producer↔schema tie: spec/test-schemas.mjs; validator: spec/validate-fingerprint.mjs validateUserConfiguration; derivation from the A-home: user-config.js.

phaedo_protocol_version.description: Protocol version this document conforms to (MAJOR.MINOR).

configuration_id.description: Stable identifier for this configuration instance (UUID v4).

subject_id.description: Same opaque identifier used by the paired fingerprint.

fingerprint_id.description: The fingerprint this configuration is paired with (§5.4). Required — a configuration without a paired fingerprint is invalid in v0.1.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of configuration creation.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of most recent update.

standing_instructions.description: Ordered list of standing instructions (§5.2) — the migrated home of the fingerprint A-home standing_rules. Same entry shape (kind discriminator + optional decision binding, Proposal 0007); injected verbatim in priority order, before fingerprint material (§5.4).

example_corpus.description: Reference outputs the subject marked exemplary (§5.3). Soft cap 20 examples (SHOULD, not enforced here). Consumers SHOULD treat as a retrieval source, not a verbatim dump. Example content is authored CONTENT by definition — the §4.6 episodic rail does not apply to it.

label.description: Short description for indexing and display.

content.description: The sample. UTF-8. v0.1 limit: 8000 characters.

tags.description: Producer- or user-assigned tags for retrieval.

extensions.description: Reserved for producer-specific extensions. Same rules as fingerprint extensions (§4.5); excluded from the canonical form (§6.1).

revoked_instructions.description: §5.2 revocation tombstones. A standing instruction the subject REMOVED. A union merge cannot express a deletion, so without these any peer still holding the rule restores it. A consumer MUST drop any instruction whose identity appears here, at READ time as well as at merge time — a device that has not merged since the revocation still holds the rule. Capped by COUNT, never pruned by age: an age prune lets a device that synced before it resurrect the rule.

key.description: The instruction's content identity. Frozen format — a change silently stops every existing tombstone matching its rule.

at.description: When the subject revoked it. Used only for cap eviction (oldest first), never as an expiry.

standing_instruction.description: The §5.2 standing-instruction entry — the ONE authored-rule shape (Proposal 0007). Canonical here; fingerprint.schema.json standing_rules[] (v0.1 A-home) $refs this def so the homes stay in lockstep through the v0.2 migration. kind:'instruction' is a verbatim rule, optionally bound to a Decision&Risk dimension via decision (which marks that dimension authored-canonical in §4.7 resolution). kind:'authorization' is a deterministic §10.5 gate (match/effect, shared $defs); if it also carries text it injects too.

text.description: Verbatim rule (§5.2). UTF-8, NFC. Injected as-is — MUST NOT be summarized. Required for instruction; optional for authorization (present → the gate also injects).

scope.description: §5.2 scope. `global` (or absent) = always active. v0.2 (OQ5): `domain` activates only for sessions/actions whose domain matches scope_domains; `task` activates only when the session's task_hint matches scope_tasks. Deterministic consumers (§10 consultation, layer selection) treat an unmatched or unknown context as INACTIVE (fail-closed); a model-mediated injection consumer with NO session context instead renders the rule with an explicit conditional scope prefix, delegating activation to the consuming model (§5.2 activation rules).

scope_domains.description: DOMAIN scope only (required when scope='domain') — the domains this instruction activates for. Same case-insensitive substring namespace as action_descriptor.domain / match.domains / session_context.domain: the instruction is active when the session's domain string CONTAINS one of these entries (lowercased).

scope_tasks.description: TASK scope only (required when scope='task') — task descriptors this instruction activates for, matched case-insensitively as substrings of the session's task_hint (§9.2).

priority.description: §5.2 ordering hint; lower injects first. Ties broken by created_at.

decision.description: OPTIONAL (instruction). Binding to one Decision&Risk dimension; present → the projection/consultation treats it authored-canonical (§4.7 'authored overrides inferred').

polarity.description: §4.3. A negative authored rule is canonical over a contradicting inferred positive.

value.description: OPTIONAL catalog value token for the bound dimension (e.g. `quality`, `ask`, `more_cautious`). Carried when the rule came from a selected template (`source:"interview_template"`); lets a future resolver bind a precise value rather than just a cautious nudge. Free-text / edited rules omit it.

domain.description: OPTIONAL domain scope, same case-insensitive substring namespace as action_descriptor.domain / match.domains.

origin.description: OPTIONAL — the act-for-me vs act-as-me channel (mirrors signals[].origin). Absent/`self` = how the subject decides themselves. `delegation` = how they want an agent to act on their behalf — carried when the rule was endorsed from a delegation-promoted suggestion (`source:"delegation_promotion"`), so the resolver/projection treat it as the act-as-me preference for that dimension.

match.description: AUTHORIZATION only — §10.5 matcher. Optional (matchless = matches all).

effect.description: AUTHORIZATION only — §10.5 effect. Required when kind=authorization.

note.description: AUTHORIZATION only — resolver rationale_hint source (back-compat with consult_policies.note).

expires_at.description: AUTHORIZATION only — OPTIONAL RFC 3339. Conditional/revocable authority (§10.5): the authorization lapses (stops applying) once this instant passes. ENFORCED (authority-narrowing, fail-safe).

agents.description: AUTHORIZATION only — OPTIONAL, ENFORCED (§10.5). Scope to specific PAIRED CLIENTS: opaque phone-issued `client_id` values, compared exactly, matched against the RESOLVER'S OWN pairing identity — never the self-asserted `agent_id`. ENFORCED for authority-expanding effects (`autoproceed`, `bias_bold`) only; restrictive rules apply regardless of scope. Authority-narrowing, like `expires_at` and `require_binding`: unlisted or unpaired means the rule does not apply, never that it applies more broadly. ABSENT ≠ EMPTY: omitting the field leaves the rule unscoped (every client); an empty array is a scope naming no client and matches none. An authoring surface that deselects every client MUST write [] rather than omit the field. Entries MUST be strings; non-strings are dropped, not coerced.

require_binding.description: AUTHORIZATION only — OPTIONAL (§10.5). Apply this rule only to requests carrying a valid §10.2 `action_binding`. ENFORCED for authority-expanding effects (`autoproceed`, `bias_bold`) only; restrictive rules apply regardless. Authority-narrowing, like `expires_at`.

source.description: OPTIONAL provenance: how the rule was authored — hand-written in onboarding (`interview`), endorsed from a selected seed template in onboarding (`interview_template`), by endorsing a delta-promoted inferred-pattern suggestion (`delta_promotion`), by endorsing a delegation-promoted suggestion built from the subject's consult override history (`delegation_promotion`, an act-as-me rule), or by endorsing an autonomy-promoted §10.5 `autoproceed` authorization built from a class of actions the subject repeatedly and deliberately approved (`autonomy_promotion`, §10.7). All are authored: endorsement is the write.
